units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
quite touched.
Oh, that's poetry, Tavy, real poetry. It gives me that strange sudden sense of an echo from a former existence which always seems to me such a striking proof that we have immortal souls.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Do you believe that is true?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Tavy, if it is to become true you must lose me as well as love me.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Oh!
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: he hastily sits down at the little table and covers his face with his hands.
with conviction.
Tavy: I wouldn't for worlds destroy your illusions. I can neither take you nor let you go. I can see exactly what will suit you. You must be a sentimental old bachelor for my sake.
units.name: ANN

units.text: desperately.
Ann: I'll kill myself.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Oh no you won't: that wouldn't be kind. You won't have a bad time. You will be very nice to women; and you will go a good deal to the opera. A broken heart is a very pleasant complaint for a man in London if he has a comfortable income.
units.name: ANN

units.text: considerably cooled, but believing that he is only recovering his self-control.
I know you mean to be kind, Ann. Jack has persuaded you that cynicism is a good tonic for me.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: He rises with quiet dignity.
studying him slyly.
You see, I'm disillusionizing you already. That's what I dread.
units.name: ANN

units.text: You do not dread disillusionizing Jack.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: her face lighting up with mischievous ecstasy--whispering.

I can't: he has no illusions about me. I shall surprise Jack the other way. Getting over an unfavorable impression is ever so much easier than living up to an ideal. Oh, I shall enrapture Jack sometimes!
units.name: ANN

units.text: resuming the calm phase of despair, and beginning to enjoy his broken heart and delicate attitude without knowing it.
I don't doubt that. You will enrapture him always. And he--the fool!--thinks you would make him wretched.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Yes: that's the difficulty, so far.
units.name: ANN

units.text: heroically.
Shall I tell him that you love him?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: quickly.
Oh no: he'd run away again.
units.name: ANN

units.text: shocked.
Ann: would you marry an unwilling man?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: What a queer creature you are, Tavy! There's no such thing as a willing man when you really go for him.
units.name: ANN

units.text: She laughs naughtily.
I'm shocking you, I suppose. But you know you are really getting a sort of satisfaction already in being out of danger yourself.
units.name: ANN

units.text: OCTAVIUS [startled] Satisfaction! [Reproachfully] You say that to me!
Well, if it were really agony, would you ask for more of it?
units.name: ANN

units.text: Have I asked for more of it?
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: You have offered to tell Jack that I love him. That's self-sacrifice, I suppose; but there must be some satisfaction in it. Perhaps it's because you're a poet. You are like the bird that presses its breast against the sharp thorn to make itself sing.
units.name: ANN

units.text: It's quite simple. I love you; and I want you to be happy. You don't love me; so I can't make you happy myself; but I can help another man to do it.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Yes: it seems quite simple. But I doubt if we ever know why we do things. The only really simple thing is to go straight for what you want and grab it. I suppose I don't love you, Tavy; but sometimes I feel as if I should like to make a man of you somehow. You are very foolish about women.
units.name: ANN

units.text: almost coldly.
I am content to be what I am in that respect.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: Then you must keep away from them, and only dream about them. I wouldn't marry you for worlds, Tavy.
units.name: ANN

units.text: I have no hope, Ann: I accept my ill luck. But I don't think you quite know how much it hurts.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: You are so softhearted! It's queer that you should be so different from Violet. Violet's as hard as nails.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Oh no. I am sure Violet is thoroughly womanly at heart.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: with some impatience.
Why do you say that? Is it unwomanly to be thoughtful and businesslike and sensible? Do you want Violet to be an idiot--or something worse, like me?
units.name: ANN
